questions.problem: Given \(f(x)=6x^3-16x^2+2\) and \(g(x)=x^2-3x+1\), compute \(f(x)\cdot g(x)\) and write in standard form.
questions.error_label: FORGOT TO DISTRIBUTE THE CONSTANT TERM
questions.error_note: Kai distributed \(6x^3\) and \(-16x^2\) through \(g(x)\) but completely skipped the \(+2\) term. The missing piece: \(2(x^2-3x+1)=2x^2-6x+2\). That accounts for the three missing terms. When multiplying polynomials, every term of the first must hit every term of the second — easy to lose a constant at the end.

questions.problem: Sketch a degree-5 polynomial satisfying six conditions. Part 4: the sketch must show a relative minimum at \(x=-3\).
questions.kai_answer: Curve goes UP through \(x=-3\) with no valley — no relative min present.
questions.correct_answer: The sketch should dip DOWN to form a valley (local minimum) at \(x=-3\), then rise again.
questions.error_note: Kai's curve passes through the \(x=-3\) region going upward with no dip at all. A relative minimum means the curve must come down, reach a low point at \(x=-3\), and then go back up — forming a valley. When sketching from a checklist of conditions, tick off each one on the finished sketch to make sure none were missed.

questions.problem: Write a polynomial with x-intercepts \(-3,\; 1,\; 5\) that passes through \((-1,-3)\) and \((3,3)\).
questions.error_label: SIGN ERRORS ON TWO FACTORS + MISSING LEADING COEFFICIENT
questions.error_note: Two problems here. First, Kai reversed the signs: wrote \((x-3)\) for the root \(x=-3\) and \((x+1)\) for the root \(x=1\). Remember: root \(r\) → factor \((x - r)\), so root \(-3\) → \((x-(-3))=(x+3)\), and root \(1\) → \((x-1)\). Second, Kai never found the leading coefficient \(c\). Plug a known point like \((-1,-3)\) into \(c(x+3)(x-1)(x-5)\) and solve: \(c(2)(-2)(-6)=24c=-3\), so \(c=-\tfrac{1}{8}\).
questions.coaching_note: The \(c=-\tfrac{1}{8}\) work visible on the paper was done during post-test corrections with Marcus, not during the original test.

questions.problem: From the graph of \(R\) (a W-shaped degree-4 polynomial with positive leading coefficient), identify all relative extrema.
questions.correct_answer: Relative min at \((-4,\,-3)\), relative max at \((-2,\,0)\), relative min at \((1,\,-5)\)
questions.error_label: EXTREMA NOT WRITTEN AS COORDINATE POINTS
questions.error_note: Kai listed raw numbers instead of \((x, y)\) coordinate pairs. The y-values \(-5\), \(-3\), \(0\) are the right magnitudes but jumbled up, and the x-coordinates are missing entirely. Relative extrema are points on the graph — always write them as \((x, y)\) pairs. Read the x-coordinate and y-coordinate separately from the graph for each peak or valley.

Kai expanded \((x-3)^2\) with \((-3)(-3)=-9\) instead of \(+9\). The correct expansion: \((x-3)^2 = x^2 - 6x + 9\). This sign error cascaded through the rest of the multiplication, flipping signs on every subsequent term. When squaring a binomial, always use \((a-b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2\) — the last term is always positive.
